findings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes) contains extensive Electric Transmission Notes (Block 20) that reference transmission structures, transmission easements, and transmission wires with specific safety and clearance requirements (no digging within 25 feet of structures, 20-foot clearance from energized lines, etc.). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) depicts an overhead electric line marked '- OHE -' with utility poles along the southern property boundary, crossing at proposed driveway entrances. Sheet 21 (Electrical Design) shows 4 transformer pads and multiple meters distributed throughout the site. However, the Master Comment Report (Electric Review section) cites a Bluebeam review link (https://studio.bluebeam.com/share/epcafnizivuefw) for Austin Energy review comments but no evidence of AE transmission engineering review completion is documented in the submitted site plan materials. The applicability note for EL-20.5 requires checking for 'transmission easements, substantially larger pole structures, or plan notes referencing transmission' - all three indicators are present on this site plan. It is unclear whether formal Austin Energy Transmission engineering review for clearances, access, and maintenance has been completed as required by UCM § 1.14.0.
findings.reasoning: The site plan contains multiple references to transmission facilities requiring coordination (Sheet 3 notes), shows overhead electric infrastructure (Sheet 9), and proposes grading and construction activities that could affect transmission facilities. UCM § 1.14.0 requires AE transmission review for projects with transmission facilities on or adjacent to the site. While transmission-related requirements are documented on Sheet 3, there is no affirmative evidence in the site plan materials that formal Austin Energy Transmission engineering review has been completed and documented. The applicability threshold of 'development adjacent to transmission lines' appears to be met, but the required review documentation is not evident in the submitted materials or the completeness check comments.
findings.comment: Site plan contains transmission facility references and overhead electric infrastructure but lacks documentation of Austin Energy Transmission engineering review for clearances, access, and maintenance as required by UCM § 1.14.0. No transmission engineering approval letter or review comments are evident in submitted materials.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows electrical meters distributed across multiple locations throughout the site, with meters located adjacent to different buildings: north side of Bldg. 1/3, space between Bldg. 2 and Bldg. 4, east side of Bldg. 5, west side of Bldg. 8, and space between Bldg. 6 and Bldg. 7. This represents at least 5-6 separate meter locations spread across the entire site rather than grouped in one common location. The plan does not label or depict any disconnect switches or show grouping of meters and disconnects at a single location. No disconnects are explicitly shown anywhere on the sheet. The scale is 1" = 20', which means the distances between these scattered meter locations would be approximately 60-100+ feet apart based on the spatial distribution visible in the drawing.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1(I) requires that meters and disconnects be grouped together in a common location with maximum 20-foot separation and line of sight. The site plan shows meters scattered across multiple buildings throughout the 2.16-acre site - a configuration that cannot comply with the 20-foot maximum distance requirement. The applicant has failed to demonstrate that meters and disconnects are grouped at a common location or that the 20-foot maximum separation is met. The absence of any labeled disconnects on the electrical design sheet, combined with the scattered meter locations, constitutes non-compliance with the grouping and distance requirements.
findings.comment: Electrical meters are scattered across multiple building locations throughout the site rather than grouped at a common location. Meters shown on Bldg. 1, Bldg. 2, Bldg. 5, Bldg. 8 areas, and spaces between buildings - separated by 60+ feet, exceeding the 20-foot maximum. No disconnects are shown on the plan. Applicant must group all meters and disconnects at a common location within 20 feet separation and line of sight.

applicableAreas: transformer pad locations near parking areas
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design) shows 4 transformer pads located at: west side near entrance drive (landscape island), southwest area near entrance (landscape island), east side central area (between Bldg. 4 and 5), and southeast area (between Bldg. 6 and 7). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows 10 surface parking spaces and 78 garage parking spaces, with surface parking primarily concentrated in the central entrance area and along the main drive aisles. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 indicated that 'None of the transformer pads appear to be within 4 feet of designated parking stalls' based on visual inspection, but the analysis noted the lack of explicit distance dimensions on the plan. Without precise distance measurements between the transformer pads and the nearest parking stalls/traffic areas, and without bollard details shown on the electrical plan, it cannot be definitively confirmed whether the 4-foot minimum clearance requirement is met at all locations.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 requires that pad-mounted equipment within 4 feet of parking or traffic areas must have 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal post bollards per AE Design equipment pad details. The site plan shows transformer locations and parking areas but does not provide dimensioned distances from pads to parking/traffic edges. While vision analysis suggested pads are not immediately adjacent to parking stalls, the lack of explicit distance callouts and the absence of any bollard details on the electrical plan create ambiguity. The requirement applies if pads are within 4 feet, but precise verification requires either: (1) detailed measurements on the plan, or (2) explicit notation that clearance exceeds 4 feet. No bollard details are shown on Sheet 21.
findings.comment: Transformer pad locations are shown on electrical design plan but distances to parking/traffic areas are not dimensioned. Bollard protection details are not shown. Verification required that all pads are either more than 4 feet from parking/traffic or that 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal post bollards are detailed per UCM § 1.10.4.

applicableAreas: grading and drainage areas around electrical equipment
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design) depicts 4 transformer pads but provides no specific drainage direction indicators, spot elevations, or grading notes showing how stormwater is directed around these pads. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) does not show transformer pad locations at all - it only shows building footprints, storm drain routing in the drive aisles, retaining walls, and drainage easements. The transformer pads are not depicted on the grading plan, creating a disconnect between the electrical design and the drainage design. General contour lines pass through the site (elevations ranging 672-690 feet) but no specific micro-drainage detail is provided for the individual transformer pads. The electrical sheet's general site contours and the grading plan's drainage flow arrows do not specifically address how drainage is directed relative to the transformer pad locations. No notation on either sheet indicates that drainage around pad-mounted equipment (particularly oil-filled transformers) is designed to flow away from buildings.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 requires that grading and drainage around oil-filled pad-mounted equipment be directed away from buildings. The site plan materials show transformer locations (Sheet 21) and site grading/drainage (Sheet 11) separately without cross-reference or specific notation demonstrating compliance. The fact that transformer pads are not depicted on the grading plan means the grading design has not explicitly addressed drainage direction around these electrical facilities. Without specific drainage callouts, arrows, or elevations tied to the transformer pads showing drainage flow direction, it cannot be verified that the requirement for drainage to flow away from buildings is met. The absence of this specification in either the electrical or grading plans constitutes unclear compliance.
findings.comment: Transformer pad locations shown on Electrical Design Plan but drainage direction around pads is not indicated on either electrical or grading plans. Grading Plan does not depict transformer pads, creating no cross-reference showing how stormwater drains relative to oil-filled equipment. Provide drainage direction indicators (arrows and spot elevations) on either the electrical or grading plan demonstrating that drainage flows away from buildings as required by UCM § 1.10.4.
